questions.stem: Energy supplied to 1 mole of monoatomic gas is 48 J and changes its temperature by $2^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Find the work done by gas.
questions.solution:
By $1^{st}$ law of thermodynamics
$\Delta Q = \Delta W + \Delta U$
$48 = W_{gas}\ \frac{3}{2} \times 1 \times \frac{25}{3} \times 2$
$\Rightarrow W_{gas} = 48 - 25$
$\Rightarrow W_{gas} = 23\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.stem: Light of wavelength $\lambda = 300\ \mathrm{nm}$ incident on a metal surface whose work function $\phi = 2.4\ \mathrm{eV}$, then find stopping potential.
If the weight of an object at surface of earth is 300 N then find the weight of object at depth R/4 from surface of the earth.
questions.solution:
$W = mg$
$300 = mg_{s} \quad \ldots(i)$
for depth
$g' = g_{s}\left[1 - \frac{d}{R}\right]$
$g' = g_{s}\left[1 - \frac{R/4}{R}\right]$
$= g_{s}[1 - 1/4]$
$g' = \frac{3}{4}g_{s}$
$W' = mg'$
$\Rightarrow W' = m\left(\frac{3}{4}g_{s}\right) \quad \ldots(2)$
Using (1) and (2)
$\frac{W'}{300} = \frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow W' = 225$

questions.stem: An EM wave is travelling along the x-axis, the equation of electric field is $E = 600\sin(kx - \omega t)$. Find out intensity of EM wave.

Two identical conducting shell having same charge are placed at finite distance. The force applied by one conductor on another is 16 N. Now an uncharged identical conducting shell is introduced such that it touch one by one the conducting shell respectively. Find out final coloumb force acting between the conducting spheres.
questions.solution:
$F = \frac{kQ^{2}}{r^{2}} = 16\ \mathrm{N}$
When it is touched with first, charge distributed in both the shell
$\frac{Q_{1}}{Q_{2}} = \frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}} \Rightarrow 1$
$Q_{1} = Q_{2} = \frac{Q}{2}$
Now the shell is touched with another
$Q_{1}' = \frac{Q}{2} + \frac{Q}{4} = \frac{3Q}{4}$
$Q_{2}' = \frac{3Q}{4}$
Now force
$F' = \frac{k\left(\frac{Q}{2}\right)\left(\frac{3Q}{4}\right)}{r^{2}} = \frac{3}{8}\left(\frac{kQ^{2}}{r^{2}}\right) \Rightarrow \frac{3}{8} \times 16 = 6\ \mathrm{N}$

questions.stem: If the maximum current is drawn from a LRC circuit of $R = 100\ \Omega$, $C = 2.5\ \mathrm{nF}$, $L = 100\ \mathrm{H}$ then find frequency in rad/sec.
questions.solution:
i is max in resonance condition.
$X_{L} = X_{C}$
$\Rightarrow \omega L = \frac{1}{\omega C}$
$\Rightarrow \omega^{2} = \frac{1}{LC}$
$\Rightarrow \omega = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$
$\Rightarrow \omega = \frac{1}{\sqrt{100 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-9}}}$
$= \frac{10^{5}}{50} = \frac{1000}{5}$
$\omega = 2000\ \mathrm{rad/sec}$.
